News22.09.26by Zainab Hussain

A Swiss private equity firm and UK investor have bought a 1,570-bed student housing portfolio for £165m #UKhousing

Bay Downing and Jessica Hardman of Aboria Capital (picture: Aboria Capital)

Partners Group, which is headquartered in Switzerland, and Aboria Capital acquired the purpose-built student accommodation (PBSA) portfolio from HSBC Asset Management for £165m.

The five-scheme portfolio is spread across Liverpool, Newcastle, London and Cambridge and is 98% let for the 2026-27 academic year.

The acquisition of the portfolio was made by a joint venture between Partners Group, Aboria Capital and two UK family offices, including the Downing Group, one of the UK’s largest privately owned property businesses.

It is the first acquisition for Aboria, which was launched in 2024 in partnership with the Downing family office. Aboria is led by Jessica Hardman, former UK chief executive of asset manager DWS, and Bay Downing, co-chief executive of Downing.

The portfolio includes The Arch in Liverpool containing 241 beds; The Electra in Liverpool containing 90 beds; The View in Newcastle containing 444 beds; The Lyra in Acton, London containing 209 beds; and The Railyard in Cambridge containing 586 beds.

Aboria said the deal reflected its focus on refurbishing “first and second-generation” PBSA stock.

The joint venture will implement a “value-creation plan” with bedroom and amenity upgrades to grow rents across the portfolio. This includes addressing specifications that are no longer meeting modern student expectations or current energy standards.

Partners Group is one of the world’s biggest private credit firms, with $186bn in global assets under management. It invested in the PBSA deal through its real estate secondaries strategy.

Henrik Orrbeck, global co-head of real estate at Partners Group, said: “We have strong conviction in this portfolio, with each of the assets strategically located across the UK’s leading university cities.

“We have a track record in the student accommodation space and continue to see strong relative value in the UK market, reflecting the country’s leading university offering and structural shortage of high-quality accommodation stock.”

Ms Hardman added: “This is an exceptional portfolio of scale and quality, made even more compelling by the depth of knowledge we already have of the assets. Our vertically integrated model means we are close to every asset from day one, aligning investment strategy with day-to-day operations.

“That allows us to protect and grow income, sustain occupancy and identify opportunities to create value throughout the investment lifecycle.”

Tim Williams, head of real estate investment at HSBC Asset Management, said: “We are pleased to complete this transaction following an extended hold period. Having acquired many of the assets through funding and development, the sale delivers a positive return of capital to our investors.”

HSBC Asset Management was advised on the deal by CBRE and Pinsent Masons.

Last week, an 813-home PBSA and co-living development project in Exeter was put on sale. The scheme has a gross development value of more than £145m and is fully consented, subject to the completion of a Section 106 agreement. It will have 399 student and 414 co-living homes.

Last month, a report by property agency Knight Frank found that PBSA construction firms are focusing almost entirely on Russell Group cities as development pressures persist. A total of 95% of UK student beds under construction and due to complete in time for the 2026-27 academic year are located in Russell Group locations.

In addition, last month two investors and a pension fund partnered with the University of Manchester to deliver a £530m student housing scheme.
